text:
morgan: Heads-up — noticed a weird mismatch between error budget burn and GPU saturation alerts this morning. EB dashboard spiked ~4% while regional gpu_saturation alerts barely triggered. Any theories? :thinking:

deepa: I saw that too. My initial guess is cardinality/label mismatch in the recording rules — the saturation metric we use for EB aggregation drops tenant label sometimes so burn gets attributed to the default bucket.

sam: Hmm. Which metrics are in the EB query? We have a couple of different gpu_* metrics floating around.

morgan: EB calc currently references recording rule `sli:gpu_saturation:ratio` (per-tenant) and falls back to `sli:gpu_saturation:region_ratio` when tenant label missing. But the alerting rule uses `node_gpu_utilization` with `gpu_id` labels. I think the join loses tenant.

lia: Can you paste the recording rule and the alert rule?

morgan: Sure — recording rule is: ```yaml
- record: sli:gpu_saturation:ratio
  expr: |
    sum by (tenant,region) (rate(gpu_device_busy_seconds_total[5m]))
    /
    sum by (tenant,region) (rate(gpu_device_total_seconds[5m]))
```

morgan: Alert rule (simplified): ```yaml
- alert: GPUHighSaturation
  expr: avg_over_time(node_gpu_utilization{job="gpu-exporter"}[5m]) > 0.88
  for: 10m
  labels:
    severity: page
```

deepa: There's the mismatch — `node_gpu_utilization` doesn't include `tenant` or `region` labels. The exporter is node-level. Our recording rule uses device metrics that are instrumented by the scheduler and include tenant and region. When we aggregate for EB we use the recording rule, but the alert is still firing on node-level and we don't map back to tenant. So EB reports look like tenant X burned but alert was on node Y.

sam: So resolution options: 1) enrich node-level metrics with `region` and best-effort `tenant` (hard), 2) change alerting to use the recording rule so alerts and EB use same aggregation, 3) change EB to rely on node-level and map tenants using allocation tables. I'm leaning to 2.

kyle: Option 2 is cleaner: use the recording rule outputs as the source of truth. But watch out for increased cardinality if we create per-gpu recording rules with both `tenant` and `region`. We already see explosion in Grafana queries.

morgan: Agreed re cardinality. For immediate fix I propose: switch alert expr to `sli:gpu_saturation:ratio` and add `for: 15m` so short spikes don't page. Then create a follow-up ticket to instrument mapping from pod allocation -> tenant in the exporter.

lia: +1. Also add a short debounce on EB ingestion: we currently compute EB on a 1h sliding window and publish every 5m; if we de-dupe small transient blips it'll be less noisy.

ops-bot: Incident policy triggered: page on any `GPUHighSaturation` firing with severity=page after 15m. (automated message)

sam: Quick sample PromQL suggestion for alerting on the recording rule: ```promql
avg by (tenant,region) (sli:gpu_saturation:ratio) > 0.85
```

deepa: Also add an `or` clause to handle missing tenant label and attribute to `region` only, so pages still go to the right oncall: ```promql
(
  avg by (tenant,region) (sli:gpu_saturation:ratio) > 0.85
)
or
(
  avg by (region) (sli:gpu_saturation:region_ratio) > 0.92
)
```

morgan: Good idea. For EB math we need to be explicit about which SLI maps to which error budget: availability EB (uptime) is separate from saturation EB (capacity). Right now both were contributing to the same global EB and that caused rapid burn. Suggest we split EB per product tier: "free" vs "paying" vs "enterprise" with different budgets and different mapping to tenant labels.

kyle: We already have `billing_tier` label on some metrics. Let's standardize: recording rules must include `tenant`, `region`, `billing_tier`. Then EB ingestion can compute per-tier burn: `sum by (billing_tier) (error_tokens_burnt)`.

lia: One more gotcha — Prometheus scrape interval is 15s for exporters but our recording rules use 5m windows. If we move alerts to recording rules we should keep window consistent to avoid missing short saturations. Recommend `avg_over_time(...[10m])` for alerts and keep EB on a longer window (1h rolling) to smooth.

sam: Sounds like an action plan. I'll open a short PR to change alert rule to use `sli:gpu_saturation:ratio` with `for: 15m` and include the `or region` fallback.

morgan: Please also add a note to the runbook (docs/grafana/slo-runbook.md) that explains label assumptions and how to debug tenant-to-node attribution. Example debug query: ```promql
# which pods owned by tenant are on this node
kube_pod_info{node="ip-10-0-3-42"} * on(pod) group_left(tenant) pod_labels{label_tenant!=""}
```

deepa: For long-term: exporter change + adding `allocation` recording rules that join scheduler allocation -> node metrics. That will allow us to compute accurate per-tenant cost and EB. I'll spin up a proposal doc after PR.

lia: Also let's add an EB alert suppression window: if EB increases > 2% in under 10m, create a ticket instead of paging for first occurrence unless combined with availability page. That reduces noisy wakeups.

kyle: Agreed. We should prototype suppression in Alertmanager using `group_interval` and `repeat_interval` plus a custom webhook to evaluate historical EB trends before escalation.

morgan: Thanks all. Action items: sam -> PR for alert change, deepa -> proposal for allocation mapping, kyle -> Alertmanager suppression prototype, lia -> runbook update. I'll champion the tenant/tier split for EB. Ping me on thread when PR is up. :thumbsup:
